a negative thyroid hormone/retinoid acid response element from the rat oxytotocin gene represses gene transcription when bound by retinoic acid receptors and that strong, constitutive VP16 transactivation domains are incapable of stimulating gene transcription from this negative response element.

In summary, our research is concerned with
how the retinoic receptor is able to regulate gene transcription.
the mechanism of transcriptional regulation by retinoic acid receptors.
the molecular mechanisms by which transcription factors regulate gene transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a DNA binding site can repress transcription even when bound by a constitutive transactivating domain.
the negative retino acid response element in rat oxytocin gene promoter restricts transcription of gene expression.
a negative DNA element itself is capable of inhibiting the function of even strong transactivation domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the negative retino acid response element is a high affinity binding site that mediates negative regulation by the retinoid X receptor and the retinoic receptor.
negative response elements are not simply a matter of sequence, but also a matter of context.
the retinoic receptor, which is a member of the steroid/thyroid hormone receptor superfamily, is capable of repressing transcription when bound to a specific promoter element.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA binding site is not simply a passive scaffold that holds a transactivation domain in close proximity to the transcriptional machinery; rather, the DNA binding site itself plays an active role in the regulation of gene transcription.

a negative response element can repress gene expression even in the presence of strong transactivation domains, suggesting that DNA binding sites can act to inhibit the function of potent constitutive transactivating proteins.
the retinoic-acid response element (RARE) in the oxytocin promoter acts as a negative response element.
